rationale: Both reviews largely miss the ground truth's core threads (missing profiling/VRAM validation evidence, WebSocket vs HTTP speed-control asymmetry, duration_factor raised inside the talker as a stage-worker exception, S2Mel/talker range mismatch and duplicated bounds) — plausibly because the reviewed snapshot already reflects post-fix state for several of these. X touches the duration_factor location (indextts2_talker.py:566-569) but for a different, tangential reason (message wording), giving it a marginal recall edge. Y's findings are more rigorously evidence-grounded, quoting verbatim source lines and CI selector commands for nearly every claim (e.g. the Spanish/Arabic normalization vs PR-body overclaim, pytestmark CI deselection), which inspires more confidence than X's dramatic but harder-to-verify 'blocking' claims (uninitialized mel_head.bias, CONCAT-accumulation bug) presented without literal source quotes. Both are highly actionable with concrete file/line fixes; X does score a verifiable win by accurately praising doc content that matches the diff (num_beams, batch non-determinism notes).
